mimose.title: MimoSe: Make Sense of Me
mimose.problemText: Traditional journaling is high-friction—irregular habits and blank-page anxiety keep self-awareness from sticking.

mimose.impactText: Owned product vision, UX, and engineering end-to-end—a calm companion that surfaces AI-driven patterns without productivity pressure.
mimose.schemaDescription: Self-led AI journaling app: Figma UX, React frontend, Spring Boot backend, and proactive AI for self-awareness.

content-platform.title: Investment Content Platform (Headless CMS)
content-platform.problemText: An editorial site needed to optimize user experience and technical SEO — without developers blocking every publish cycle.
content-platform.solutionText: Designed in Figma (wireframes → UI), defined a color and typography system, and built responsive layouts. Shipped a headless CMS admin (React, RBAC) and a Next.js storefront with SSR, metadata, JSON-LD, and sitemap — content modules and editor workflows for blogs, categories, and site-wide SEO.
content-platform.impactText: Cohesive cross-device experience; structured SEO on articles and landing pages; editorial team can self-serve content updates.
content-platform.schemaDescription: Figma-led investment content platform with headless CMS admin, responsive UI, and technical SEO on Next.js.

items.question: Who is Han Kim Thuy?
items.answer: This is the portfolio of Han Kim Thuy (Hàn Kim Thủy), also written as Thuy Han Kim or hankimthuy online. I am a UX Software Engineer based in Vietnam. You can reach me at {email}, on GitHub (hankimthuy), LinkedIn (thuyhankim), or at {siteUrl}.

items.question: Are you available for freelance UX Software Engineer work?
items.answer: Yes—outside my full-time role I take scoped freelance work remotely, with clients in Vietnam and worldwide (I work from GMT+7). Typical engagements include UX-oriented development, product discovery, and helping small teams ship user-focused products. Message me on LinkedIn with the problem, audience, and timeline—or email if you prefer.

items.question: What drives you to build products?
items.answer: I'm driven by empathy. For me, a product is simply a solution to a real human problem. My motivation comes from seeing something I've built actually reduce someone's frustration, save them time, or (like in my MimoSe project) help them understand themselves better.

items.question: Why do you focus on UX-Oriented Development?
items.answer: As a UX Software Engineer, I sit at the intersection of design and code. Focusing on UX is central to how I build—not an afterthought. I believe a 'feature' isn't 'done' when the code is merged; it's 'done' when the user can achieve their goal effortlessly. This mindset is the foundation of my product-focused approach.

items.question: Are you pursuing Product Owner roles?
items.answer: Yes—Product Owner is a career path I'm actively building toward. Today I focus on UX Software Engineer work at the design–code intersection; over time I want to own discovery, prioritization, and outcomes end to end. My Scrum background, product discovery experience, and user-first delivery all point in that direction.

items.question: How do you handle ambiguity and changing requirements?
items.answer: I embrace them—change is a core part of the Agile/Scrum process. When requirements change, I don't see it as a problem; I see it as 'new information.' My first step is to ask 'why' to understand the new business goal or user insight. Then, I collaborate with the team (PO, BA, Designers) to assess the impact, break down the new task, and re-prioritize.

items.question: How do you work with a freelance client?
items.answer: We start with a short conversation about the problem, who's affected, and what success looks like—you don't need a technical spec upfront. I help clarify scope and timing, keep communication simple, and focus on whether the solution works for real users. My goal is to solve the right need, not to impress with tools.

items.question: How can I reach you about freelance work?
items.answer: LinkedIn is the best place to start—send a message with what you're trying to solve, who it's for, and any timeline. You can also email thuyhankim@gmail.com. I will let you know if freelance collaboration is a good fit.
